name: Bloom Energy
constraint_controlled: Bloom manufactures and deploys solid oxide fuel cell systems that deliver on-site power to data centers in 12-18 months, bypassing the 5-7 year grid interconnection queue.
physics_thesis: Bloom is one of the few commercially-scaled solutions that lets hyperscalers bring AI training capacity online without waiting for utility grid connections, which are now the binding constraint on AI buildout. Their SOFC technology is differentiated, vertically manufactured, and already contracted with AEP, Equinix, and Oracle. The physics arbitrage is real: they bypass the grid queue with a manufacturable product competitors cannot replicate quickly.
key_metrics: MW of data center backlog/bookings; product gross margin; deployment lead time vs grid queue
reasoning: Bloom directly manufactures and owns the IP/factory for SOFC stacks — a genuine physical product addressing the grid bottleneck — earning a high ownership score, though it's an equipment OEM rather than an irreplaceable resource holder. Supply response is moderate-to-slow because SOFC manufacturing capacity, ceramic stack production, and permitting take 2-5 years to scale, but unlike uranium or copper it is ultimately a manufacturable good.

name: Vistra Energy
constraint_controlled: Vistra owns ~41 GW of dispatchable generation including 6.4 GW of nuclear capacity (Comanche Peak and the Energy Harbor fleet) plus large gas and coal fleets with existing grid interconnections.
physics_thesis: Vistra controls one of the largest fleets of already-interconnected, dispatchable baseload power in the US, including four nuclear reactors that are physically irreplaceable on any reasonable AI buildout timeline. Hyperscalers are signing behind-the-meter and PPA deals directly with nuclear operators (cf. Amazon-Talen, Microsoft-Constellation), and Vistra's nuclear plus ERCOT gas footprint makes it a prime counterparty. New nuclear takes 10+ years and new large gas plants face 5-7 year interconnection queues, so existing GW are the scarce asset.
key_metrics: Nuclear PPA announcements and pricing ($/MWh); ERCOT and PJM forward power curves; uncontracted nuclear/gas GW available for hyperscaler deals
reasoning: Ownership is 9 because Vistra physically owns and operates a large nuclear fleet plus interconnected gas capacity — direct control of the exact asset hyperscalers need, with only a handful of peers (Constellation, Talen, NextEra). Supply response is 9 because new nuclear is a 10+ year build and new large interconnected thermal capacity is 5-10 years even with unlimited capital, so the existing fleet cannot be meaningfully replicated near-term.

name: Constellation Energy
constraint_controlled: Largest US nuclear fleet (~22 GW) of operating, licensed, carbon-free baseload generation directly contractable by hyperscalers.
physics_thesis: Constellation owns the largest fleet of operating nuclear reactors in the US — irreplaceable 24/7 carbon-free baseload that AI hyperscalers are signing decade-plus PPAs for (e.g. Three Mile Island restart with Microsoft). New nuclear takes 10+ years and faces NRC licensing, fuel, and supply chain bottlenecks, so existing licensed gigawatts are effectively un-replicable on the AI buildout timeline. This is a textbook physics arbitrage: scarce, licensed, already-connected baseload power.
key_metrics: GW contracted to hyperscalers via PPAs; realized $/MWh on data center contracts; license extensions and uprate MW added
reasoning: Ownership is a 10 because CEG physically operates the largest licensed nuclear fleet in the US — geologically/regulatorily irreplaceable assets with no substitute for 24/7 clean baseload. Supply response is a 10 because new nuclear capacity requires 10+ years for licensing and construction even with unlimited capital, and SMRs are not yet commercially deployed at scale.

name: NRG Energy
constraint_controlled: NRG owns and operates ~13 GW of dispatchable generation capacity (gas, coal) primarily in ERCOT/Texas, plus a large retail electricity customer book.
physics_thesis: NRG controls existing, interconnected generation capacity in Texas — the most AI-data-center-hungry grid in the US — at a moment when new generation queues are 5+ years long. Its retail platform also positions it to sign long-term PPAs with hyperscalers seeking firm power. However, its fleet is largely gas/coal with retail services (Vivint) diluting the pure-play physics angle.
key_metrics: MW of dispatchable capacity in ERCOT; hyperscaler PPA announcements; ERCOT forward power prices
reasoning: Ownership score of 6 because NRG directly operates physical generation assets behind grid interconnects (a real bottleneck), but multiple IPP competitors exist (Vistra, Constellation, Talen) and a meaningful chunk of revenue is retail/smart home services rather than pure generation. Supply response of 7 reflects that new gas plants take 3-5 years and grid interconnection queues stretch 5-7 years, so existing capacity is genuinely scarce but not as irreplaceable as nuclear or uranium.

name: Core Scientific
constraint_controlled: Owns and operates ~1.2GW of energized, grid-connected data center power capacity across multiple US sites that can be converted from Bitcoin mining to AI/HPC hosting.
physics_thesis: Core Scientific controls something AI hyperscalers physically cannot get for 5-7 years: large-scale, already-energized grid interconnections. The CoreWeave 12-year, $10B+ contract validates that pre-connected power sites are the binding constraint for AI buildout. New interconnects of this scale face multi-year ISO queues regardless of capital deployed.
key_metrics: Contracted AI/HPC power capacity (MW); CoreWeave contract revenue realization; Incremental MW energized per quarter
reasoning: Core Scientific is the canonical example in this framework — it physically owns and operates the scarcest asset in the AI buildout: gigawatts of pre-existing grid interconnection. Ownership scores 9 (not 10) because a handful of other Bitcoin miners hold similar pre-connected sites. Supply response is 8 because replicating 1GW+ of new grid interconnect takes 5-7 years minimum even with unlimited capital, due to ISO queues and transmission constraints.

name: TeraWulf
constraint_controlled: TeraWulf owns and operates the Lake Mariner site in upstate New York with ~750 MW of grid-connected power (zero-carbon, nuclear/hydro-fed) being converted from bitcoin mining to AI/HPC hosting, with multi-hundred-MW leases signed to Core42/Fluidstack/Google.

reasoning: Ownership 8 because WULF physically owns and operates the Lake Mariner site with energized, low-carbon interconnection — a genuinely scarce asset with limited replicability — though it is one of several pre-connected miners (CORZ, IREN, CIFR) competing for the same thesis, keeping it below 9-10. Supply response 8 because new comparable sites require 5-7+ years of grid queue, transformer procurement, and permitting — unlimited capital cannot meaningfully accelerate the ISO interconnection process.

name: Iris Energy
constraint_controlled: Owns and operates ~2.9 GW of secured grid-connected power capacity at data center sites in Texas and British Columbia, with operational substations and energized infrastructure.

reasoning: Ownership score 8 because IREN directly owns the land, substations, and grid interconnections — a genuinely scarce physical asset with 5-7 year replication time — though it competes with several other miner-to-AI converts (CORZ, CIFR, APLD, WULF). Supply response 8 because new grid-connected gigawatt-scale sites take 5-7+ years to permit, interconnect, and energize regardless of capital.

name: Applied Digital
constraint_controlled: Operates data center sites in North Dakota with secured power capacity (400MW+ at Ellendale) and grid interconnects for HPC/AI hosting.

name: Riot Platforms
constraint_controlled: Riot operates large-scale, grid-connected power capacity at its Rockdale (Texas) and Corsicana facilities, totaling ~1+ GW of contracted/energized power that bypasses multi-year interconnection queues.

Supply response score 7 reflects that replicating a 1 GW ERCOT-interconnected site takes 4-7 years given transformer lead times and interconnection queues, though Texas is faster than most US grids.

name: Marathon Digital
constraint_controlled: Owns and operates large-scale energized data center sites with grid-connected power capacity (~1+ GW) currently used for Bitcoin mining, convertible to AI/HPC hosting.

Supply response of 6 reflects that new grid-connected gigawatt sites take 2-5 years to build and energize, though existing miners worldwide create some near-term substitutes for the pre-connected power thesis.

name: Eaton Corporation
constraint_controlled: Eaton manufactures medium- and low-voltage switchgear, transformers, busways, and power distribution units that data centers physically cannot operate without.

Supply response score 7: ramping switchgear and transformer capacity requires 2-5 years due to grain-oriented electrical steel shortages, skilled labor, and certification/testing cycles, but it is not geologically constrained like mining.

name: GE Vernova
constraint_controlled: Dominant manufacturing capacity for heavy-duty gas turbines and high-voltage grid equipment (transformers, switchgear) with multi-year backlogs.

As grid capex surges, Quanta's labor pool is a genuine physical bottleneck, though it is a service provider rather than an owner of irreplaceable hard assets.

reasoning: Ownership score of 6: Quanta directly operates the scarce asset (skilled labor + specialized fleet) rather than just selling equipment, but it does not own irreplaceable physical infrastructure like mines or generation, and competitors (MasTec, MYR Group) exist. Supply response of 6 reflects 2-5 year lead times to expand specialty grid equipment manufacturing (tooling, skilled labor, grain-oriented steel, copper) — real but not insurmountable bottlenecks.

name: Vertiv Holdings
constraint_controlled: Vertiv is the dominant OEM for liquid cooling and integrated power management systems required by high-density AI GPU clusters that physically cannot be air-cooled.
physics_thesis: Blackwell-class and beyond GPUs dissipate heat densities that exceed air-cooling physics, forcing a hard transition to direct-liquid and immersion cooling. Vertiv has the deepest installed base, reference designs co-developed with NVIDIA, and the manufacturing scale for CDUs, rear-door heat exchangers, busbars, and switchgear — components every hyperscaler needs simultaneously. While competitors (Schneider, nVent, Munters) exist, Vertiv's integrated power+thermal stack and lead times give it pricing power as data center thermal load is a non-negotiable physical constraint.
key_metrics: Liquid cooling backlog and book-to-bill; AI-related orders growth YoY; gross margin expansion on thermal segment
reasoning: Ownership score of 9 reflects that Vertiv is explicitly cited as the dominant liquid-cooling supplier in the rubric — it manufactures the irreplaceable thermal infrastructure, though 2-3 credible competitors prevent a perfect 10. Supply response of 6 because while Vertiv itself can scale factories in 2-3 years, qualifying new entrants into hyperscaler reference designs, scaling specialized CDU/manifold manufacturing, and copper/compressor supply chains make rapid substitution difficult.

name: Modine Manufacturing
constraint_controlled: Modine manufactures and operates production capacity for data center cooling systems (CDUs, chillers, air handlers) including the Airedale brand, a key supplier for AI/HPC thermal management.

While not the dominant liquid-cooling OEM (Vertiv holds that crown), Modine has a fast-growing data center segment with real manufacturing footprint and customer lock-in. The bottleneck is genuine but Modine is one of several credible suppliers, not a sole-source.

Cameco controls irreplaceable high-grade Canadian reserves and is one of only a handful of Western producers — there is no substitute material and no fast supply response. Westinghouse adds reactor OEM exposure, doubling the lock on the nuclear value chain.

Supply response is also a 10 because new uranium mines require 10-20 years for exploration, permitting, and development regardless of capital, and the fuel cycle (conversion, enrichment) adds further bottlenecks.

name: Oklo Inc.
constraint_controlled: Oklo is developing Aurora SMR fission powerhouses (15-75MW) but has not yet built or operated any commercial reactor.

The thesis is real but speculative: it's a design/developer stage company, not yet a power asset owner.

Supply response score of 9 reflects that fission plants, even SMRs, take 5-10+ years to license, fuel (HALEU constrained), and build, and cannot be accelerated meaningfully with capital alone.

reasoning: SCCO directly owns and operates physically scarce, geologically irreplaceable copper deposits — pure physical control of the bottleneck, not equipment or services. reasoning: Ownership score of 4 reflects that NVIDIA is fabless and owns no physical bottleneck infrastructure — its scarcity is IP/software, not physics. Supply response of 6 reflects that competitors (AMD, custom ASICs from hyperscalers) need 2-5 years to meaningfully challenge CUDA and the architectural lead, but this is a software/design moat, not a geological or grid-based one.

Supply response of 5 because GPU cloud capacity can be replicated by hyperscalers and competitors (Lambda, Nebius, hyperscalers) within 1-2 years given capital and Nvidia allocation.

reasoning: Intel directly owns and operates leading-edge fabs — a genuine physical bottleneck with only 2-3 global competitors, fitting the 6-7 band. reasoning: Lumentum genuinely operates physical InP wafer fabs producing scarce laser chips for AI interconnects, which lifts ownership above a pure designer — but it faces real competition from Coherent, Broadcom, and Marvell, capping it at 6. reasoning: Ownership score of 5 reflects that SanDisk does physically operate fabs (real infrastructure) but NAND is not a true AI bottleneck and faces 4+ scaled competitors, so it's exposure rather than control. Supply response of 6 reflects realistic 2-5 year fab buildout timelines, but the industry can also flex existing capacity within ~1 year, capping the score.

name: Coherent Corp
constraint_controlled: Manufactures high-speed optical transceivers, indium phosphide lasers, and photonic components essential for AI cluster networking (800G/1.6T).

reasoning: Coherent physically owns InP fabs, VCSEL production, and transceiver assembly — direct control of a bottleneck asset, but with real competition from Lumentum, Marvell/Inphi, and emerging Chinese suppliers, placing it in the 6-7 band. name: Solaris Energy Infrastructure
